after: ## What the brief says, and what it leaves to your teacher
alt: A bar shows the individual oral as the only internal component, 25 percent and 30 marks, against 75 percent for the external papers. Cards give the stimulus: a visual image at SL and an excerpt from a literary work at HL. The brief sets the same outline at both levels; timings, stages, rules on notes and criteria come from your teacher.
caption: One internal component worth 25%: an image at SL, a literary excerpt at HL.

alt: Three overlapping circles labelled receptive (understand the stimulus and questions), productive (speak at length in an organised way) and interactive (a real exchange, not memorised answers) meet at the centre labelled Oral. A note highlights the verb respond in the assessment objective.
caption: Understand, speak at length and respond: the oral tests all three skills at once.

after: ## SL: working with a visual image
alt: Four numbered layers for an SL image, each with a worked example: literal (a girl follows a recipe on a video call), theme (identities, with experiences in reserve), lens (a possible question about language and culture), and culture (compare a target-language food tradition). A strong opening sentence moves from description straight to an idea.
caption: Literal, theme, lens, culture: keep the description short and reach an idea fast.

after: ## HL: working with a literary extract
alt: Four numbered questions for an HL extract with a worked example: where is it in the work; what happens (Nadia delays replying to her mother's letter); how is it written (the untranslatable word for home, the repeated Tomorrow, the tram timetable); and why it matters (identities and experiences, with a possible question as a lens).
caption: Place it, say what happens, show how it is written, and link it to the work and a theme.

alt: Five linked boxes: frame, describe, interpret, connect and close. A bar shows describing as the shortest move and interpreting and connecting taking most of the time. Signposting phrases such as first I'll describe and this connects to sit below.
caption: Frame, describe, interpret, connect, close: keep description short and signpost each move.

alt: A teacher question with a weak yes answer is extended in three linked parts: answer, reason and example (a class clothes swap that the whole school now runs). Four cards give conversation moves with target phrases: repair by paraphrasing, clarify, agree or disagree or qualify, and buy time.
caption: Extend every answer with a reason and an example; repair, clarify and qualify in the target language.

alt: An image of a river clean-up under Sharing the planet branches to two other themes: Identities (what young people value) and Experiences (a community event that changed someone).
caption: One stimulus can lead the conversation into other themes.
